title: HEAPr: Hessian-based Efficient Atomic Expert Pruning in Output Space
claim: Experts decompose into indivisible atomic units, so pruning can cut at finer granularity than whole experts.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right zoom-in, dashed scissor cut lines through weight blocks
description: A legend at top left shows two 3D block icons, a yellow one labeled Atomic Expert 1 and a blue one labeled Atomic Expert 3. At bottom left, a rounded beige box labeled Expert has a hollow arrow marked Internal View pointing into a large rounded rectangle titled Atomic Expert Pruning. Inside, the gated feed-forward structure is drawn: W^gate and W^up are stacks of 3D columns, with blue and yellow columns side by side. The two branches pass through an Act box and merge at a multiplication node. They feed W^down, drawn as stacked blue and yellow row blocks. A vertical dashed line with scissors cuts through the columns of W^gate and W^up. A horizontal dashed line with scissors cuts through W^down. The caption Atomic Expert level sits below. Blue and yellow carry the identity of each atomic expert.

abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures in large language models (LLMs) deliver exceptional performance and reduced inference costs compared to dense LLMs. However, their large parameter counts result in prohibitive memory requirements, limiting practical deployment. While existing pruning methods primarily focus on expert-level pruning, this coarse granularity often leads to substantial accuracy degradation. In this work, we introduce HEAPr, a novel pruning algorithm that decomposes experts into smaller, indivisible atomic experts, enabling more precise and flexible atomic expert pruning. To measure the importance of each atomic expert, we leverage second-order information based on principles similar to the Optimal Brain Surgeon theory. To address the computational and storage challenges posed by second-order information, HEAPr exploits the inherent properties of atomic experts to transform the second-order information from expert parameters into that of atomic expert parameters, and further simplifies it to the second-order information of atomic expert outputs. This approach reduces the space complexity from $O(d^4)$, where $d$ is the model's dimensionality, to $O(d^2)$. HEAPr requires only two forward passes and one backward pass on a small calibration set to compute the importance of atomic experts. Extensive experiments on MoE models, including DeepSeek MoE and Qwen MoE family, demonstrate that HEAPr outperforms existing expert-level pruning methods across a wide range of pruning ratios and benchmarks. Specifically, HEAPr achieves nearly lossless compression at pruning ratios of 20% ~ 25% in most models, while also reducing FLOPs nearly by 20%. The code can be found at [https://github.com/LLIKKE/HEAPr](https://github.com/LLIKKE/HEAPr).
